label: Design 4 - Kitchen-Kept Social Spine Rebuild
summary: A kitchen-preserving architectural reset that treats kitchen/dining, deck, Bedroom 2, service rooms, current lounge, and sunroom as one connected social-spine redesign.
room_changes: The renovated kitchen is retained unless minor threshold or opening work is essential.
Kitchen/dining opens more deliberately to the deck and back-side living route.
Bedroom 2 and the service end can become a new back lounge/day room.
Laundry and WC move toward separated service rooms on the office/bathroom side.
The current lounge becomes media, guest overflow, or secondary quiet living.
The sunroom is removed, reduced, or replaced by a proper bedroom depending on the final concept.
daylight_strategy: Use the deck/back/service side for daily social life while protecting the kitchen investment.
Design deck cover/shade so it improves outdoor use without darkening kitchen/dining.
Avoid making the kitchen the only good social space.
movement_strategy: Create a clearer social route from garage/back arrival to kitchen, deck, and lounge.
Separate daytime social flow from quieter evening/media use.
build_scope: Internal wall and opening changes around kitchen/dining, Bedroom 2, entrance, laundry, and lounge.
Laundry/WC relocation into separated service rooms.
Deck threshold, shade, and wind-control design.
Possible sunroom demolition or replacement with a new bedroom envelope.
risks: This is close to a full architectural renovation.
It could become expensive quickly if kitchen protection still requires adjacent structural work.
Staging matters: partial work could lock in the wrong final layout.
Professional concept drawings and structural review are needed early.
cost_notes: Broad planning band: NZD 280k to 500k+ if sunroom replacement and service-room relocation are included.
